🏛️ State of Utah Water Applications • Executive Overview

One Front Door & Smart Badge for Utah Water Systems

How our new centralized Login & Access Control Service replaces 40+ aging, disconnected permission lists with a modern, automated security system built for State staff, River Commissioners, Water Suppliers, and the Public.

🪪
The Everyday Analogy: From 40 Metal Keys to One Smart Building Badge

Previously, every water application kept its own separate clipboard of who was allowed inside. Now, Utah has one central security desk that checks your identity (UtahID or Partner Login) and issues a temporary smart badge programmed for your exact river basin, regional office, and season.

Database Consolidation
4 Silos → 1 Hub

Unifies wrsysDB, DVRTEDIT, Water Use, and HydroServer into one central system.

Role Simplification
62 Roles → 1 Role

Replaces 62 hardcoded river role names with 1 reusable Commissioner role tied to a river boundary.

Session Security
15-Min Passes

Eliminates public Wi-Fi IP hijacking with encrypted, short-lived digital passes per user.

Governance & Audit
100% Traceable

Every permission records who approved it, why, and automatically expires when seasonal work ends.

Slide 2 • Business Case

Why Change? 5 Real Risks in Our Legacy Systems

Source: 2026 DWRi Technical Debt & Roles Assessment
1. The "Conference Wi-Fi" Login Flaw High Security Risk

What happened: The legacy login system recorded a user's building internet address (IP) in a table to remember they were logged in.
Why it matters: If a staff member logged in from a hotel, conference, or shared network, anyone else on that same Wi-Fi could open the site and inherit their identity and edit privileges.

2. Four Disconnected Permission Islands Operational Bottleneck

What happened: Staff permissions were scattered across 4 separate databases (wrsysDB, DVRTEDIT, Water Use, HydroServer).
Why it matters: Onboarding or offboarding an employee meant checking 4 different systems with no unified dashboard or shared rules.

3. "101 Manual Rows" & Permission Creep Admin Overload

What happened: There was no concept of "Staff Groups." Setting up 6 Regional Office employees required typing 101 individual permission rows.
Why it matters: Over time, permissions were never cleaned up—just two veteran staff members held 30% of all access grants across the division.

4. 62 Copy-Pasted River Roles & No Expiration Audit & Compliance Gap

What happened: Because the old database couldn't say "Commissioner for Weber River," IT had to create 62 separate roles (Edit: WEBER RIVER, LOWER BEAR). Plus, seasonal deputies and contractors had no automatic expiration date.

Bottom Line for Leadership: Our goal wasn't just to write new software—it was to eliminate shared logins, stop manual data entry, and protect Utah's official water records.

Slide 3 • Core Concepts

Principle #1: Authentication vs. Authorization

Tech teams call this AuthN and AuthZ. Think of it like catching a flight at Salt Lake City International Airport:

STEP 1: AUTHENTICATION (AuthN) 🛂

"Who are you?"

Airport Equivalent: Showing your Driver's License or Passport at the TSA security desk to prove your identity.

How our solution handles it:
  • State Employees & Citizens: Log in through official UtahID.
  • Water Suppliers & Cities: Can log in with their own Microsoft or Google work accounts.
  • Scientists (USGS / Universities): Can log in with research credentials (ORCID).
  • Zero Password Liability: Our water apps never store or manage user passwords.
STEP 2: AUTHORIZATION (AuthZ) 🎫

"What are you allowed to do?"

Airport Equivalent: Scanning your Boarding Pass at Gate B14. Being inside the airport doesn't mean you can board any plane or enter the cockpit!

How our solution handles it:
  • Job Role Check: Are you a Water Commissioner, Engineer, or Public Reader?
  • Geographic Boundary: Are you assigned to the Weber River or the Sevier River?
  • Time & Safety Check: Is your seasonal deputy appointment currently active? Did you verify 2-Factor Authentication (MFA) before deleting sensor data?
1. User Logs Into UtahID / Partner ID ➔ 2. Security Hub Issues 15-Min App Badge ➔ 3. Water App Checks Badge on Every Action ➔ 4. Action Approved & Logged
📊 Visual Architecture: Two-Stage Zero Trust Flow on Google Cloud 🔍 Click diagram to enlarge
🎙️ Presenter Talking Point: "Why separate these two steps? Because UtahID is great at telling us *who* someone is—say, Kent Wilkerson. But UtahID doesn't know that Kent is the appointed Water Commissioner for the Weber River and that he delegated a seasonal deputy until October 31st. Our service bridges that gap."
Slide 4 • Security Philosophy

Principle #2: What "Zero Trust" Means in Plain English

"Zero Trust" doesn't mean we distrust our staff—it means the computer system never assumes access based on where you sit.

🏰 Old Approach: "Castle-and-Moat"

Like a medieval castle: once you cross the drawbridge (or log in from an office IP address), you can wander into almost any room all day long.

❌ Shared IP addresses treated as identity
❌ Broad permissions across all rivers or stations
❌ Temporary access stays active forever if forgotten
🛡️ New Approach: "Zero Trust Smart Badge"

Like a modern high-security hotel or hospital: your badge is checked at every door, works only for your assigned floor, and deactivates automatically at checkout time.

✅ Verifies identity, application, and river basin on every click
✅ High-risk actions (like deleting raw sensor data) require MFA
✅ Seasonal & contractor badges expire automatically on schedule
1. Default Closed

Unless a rule explicitly grants access, the door stays locked automatically.

2. Emergency Brake (Deny Override)

An explicit "Deny" rule always wins—ensuring strict separation of duties.

3. App-Specific Badges

A badge issued for the Water Map App cannot be replayed against another state system.

4. Built-in Expiration

Every seasonal deputy or consultant grant carries a start and end date enforced to the second.

🎙️ Presenter Talking Point: "When state or federal cybersecurity standards ask if our applications follow 'Zero Trust Architecture,' this slide is the exact answer. We don't rely on network location alone; we verify the person, the specific water resource, and the security context every time."
Slide 5 • Smart Access Formula

Principle #3: How We Eliminated 62 Copy-Pasted Roles

Instead of inventing a new role name for every river and office, every access grant combines three simple building blocks:

1. ROLE (What You Do)

Job Function

Defines a reusable bundle of capabilities based on a person's job—not where they work.

👷 Water Commissioner
⚙️ Automation Engineer
🚰 Public Water Supplier
2. SCOPE (Where It Applies)

Organizational or Geographic Boundary

Restricts that role to a specific level of Utah's organization tree or a single river system:

Statewide: All of DWRi / DWRe
Regional Office Tree: e.g., Northern Region (Logan) & its sub-teams
Single Resource: e.g., Weber River or Jordan Valley Water District
3. GUARDRAILS (Conditions)

Real-Time Safety Checks

Optional safety rules (called Attribute-Based Access Control) checked at the moment of the click:

🔐 2-Factor (MFA) Required: For deleting raw sensor data or editing cell modem IPs
📅 Seasonal Window: Active Apr 15 – Oct 31 only
🏛️ Employee Type: Must be verified State Employee
Real DWRi Example (Seasonal Deputy Commissioner):
Role: Water Commissioner + Scope: Weber River Only + Dates: Apr 15 – Oct 31, 2026

Slide 8 • Technology Stack Explained

Plain-English Technology Translator for Managers

Why we chose these specific industry-standard technologies—and what they mean for budget, reliability, and staffing:

1. Go (Golang) The Engine

What it is: A fast, straightforward programming language created at Google for cloud infrastructure.
Manager Benefit: Starts up in milliseconds, uses a fraction of the memory of older languages (lowering monthly cloud bills), and is rock-solid with minimal maintenance.

2. Google Cloud Run Auto-Scaling Hosting

What it is: Managed "serverless" hosting in Google Cloud.
Manager Benefit: Automatically adds capacity during peak spring runoff or drought reporting, and scales down at night. No physical servers for staff to patch or reboot, and you only pay when requests are running.

3. Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (with ltree) The Org-Chart Vault

What it is: The world's most trusted open-source enterprise database, managed by Google Cloud with automated backups.
Manager Benefit: Uses a built-in hierarchy feature (ltree) that mirrors Utah's exact organizational chart (State → DNR → DWRi → 7 Regional Offices) so regional managers automatically cover their sub-teams.

4. OIDC & Token Exchange (RFC 8693) Universal Digital Passport

What it is: Official banking- and government-grade security standards for login and digital badges.
Manager Benefit: Allows seamless login with UtahID for employees while letting external water districts, federal partners (USGS/BOR), and universities use their own existing logins safely.

🎙️ Presenter Talking Point: "Every technology here was chosen for three reasons: alignment with State of Utah GCP standards, low ongoing operating cost, and avoiding proprietary vendor lock-in. PostgreSQL, Go, and OIDC are open standards supported everywhere."
Slide 9 • Strategic Return on Investment

How This Accelerates Every Future Utah Water Project

Building this as a shared common service pays dividends across both DWRi and DWRe:

🚀

1. Faster App Delivery ("Plug & Play")

Future map portals, dashboards, and mobile tools no longer waste months building custom login screens and permission tables. They connect to this hub in days using a ready-made toolkit.

⚡

2. No Code Changes to Add Apps or Roles

Registering a brand-new application, adding a new river distribution system, or delegating a seasonal deputy is done dynamically through the admin interface—without waiting for a software deployment.

📋

3. Instant Legislative Audit Readiness

When legislative auditors or security officers ask "Who can modify water records and why?", managers can pull a complete report showing every user, approver, business justification, and expiration date.
